request: mix: 文章中のURLの全角文字・空白・末尾の句読点混入を検出する / ファイルまたは標準入力のテキストから http:// や https:// で始まるURLを探し、問題のあるものを行番号・列番号付きで報告する。問題とは、URL内の未エンコードの非ASCII文字（全角や日本語）、直後に貼り付いた「。」「、」「）」「」」などの全角句読点・括弧、末尾の半角のピリオドやカンマである。各問題について、行:列、元のURL、問題の種類、修正案（非ASCII部分をパーセントエンコードし、末尾の混入文字を除いたもの）を1行ずつ出力する。例：「詳細は https://example.com/資料。をご覧ください」という行は「1:4 https://example.com/資料。 全角句読点混入 → https://example.com/%E8%B3%87%E6%96%99」のように出力する。問題が1件でもあれば終了コード1にする。コマンド名は urlsnag

spec.name: urlsnag
spec.summary: urlsnag finds http:// and https:// URLs in text and reports those with unencoded non-ASCII characters or stray trailing punctuation, with line:column and a suggested fix.
behavior: B1: Input is the files named as arguments, read in order; with no arguments it reads stdin. Input is UTF-8 text split into lines at "\n"; a trailing "\r" on a line is removed. Line numbers start at 1 and restart for each file.
B2: In each line, find every URL start: the earliest occurrence of "http://" or "https://" (lowercase, exact) at or after the current position. Scanning continues after the end of each URL.

B3: From the start, the URL extends over characters until the first of: a Unicode whitespace character (including U+3000); an ASCII character among " < > (double quote, less-than, greater-than); a hiragana character (U+3040-U+309F); or the end of the line. In addition, the URL ends right after the first run of one or more characters from the set P = 。 、 ， ． ） 」 』 】 〉 》 ］ ｝ ！ ？ (those characters are included in the URL, the next character is not). All other characters, including kanji, katakana and other ASCII, are part of the URL.
B4: Trailing part: repeatedly remove from the end of the URL any character that is in P or is an ASCII period or comma. What remains is the body; the removed characters are the trailer.

B5: Problem type, chosen in this order: if the trailer contains a character from P, the type is 全角句読点混入; else if the trailer is non-empty (only ASCII . or ,), the type is 末尾句読点; else if the body contains any non-ASCII character, the type is 未エンコード非ASCII; otherwise the URL is fine and nothing is printed for it.
B6: Fix = the body with every non-ASCII character replaced by the percent-encoding of its UTF-8 bytes, each byte as %XX with uppercase hex. ASCII characters are left unchanged.

B7: For each problem URL print one line to stdout: LINE:COL, a space, the original URL (including its trailer), a space, the type, a space, "→", a space, the fix, then "\n". COL is the 1-based count of characters (runes, not bytes) before the URL start plus one. When more than one file is given, each line is additionally prefixed by the file name and a colon ("name:LINE:COL ...").
B8: Empty input, or input with no problem URLs, prints nothing and exits 0. If at least one problem was printed, exit 1 after processing all input.
B9: If a file cannot be opened or read, print "urlsnag: " followed by the error message to stderr and exit 2 immediately. An unknown flag prints a usage message to stderr and exits 2.
B10: The program has no flags of its own and makes no network access.
